title: HelperSSHSecretResult
description: The material itself, base64 (encoding/json's rendering of a byte slice). It is the ONE field on this wire that is a secret in the ordinary sense, and it is stated rather than hidden: a password has to be PRESENTED by the party holding the connection, and the helper is that party. It crosses a socket both ends own, under D12's same-UID trust boundary, it is never logged, never written down, and never returned by the helper. A passphrase does not cross at all — the coordinator is what parses a private key — which is why `purpose` exists to distinguish the two questions this op can be asked.

secret.description: The material, base64. Empty is refused rather than answered: a stored secret with nothing in it is a credential that was never finished being stored, and letting it through would present an empty password and report the server's refusal as a wrong one.
